Our philosophy

Accessibility starts
with understanding.

Accessibility begins with understanding how people experience the world—and what gets in the way of their participation.

Barriers can exist in physical spaces, digital tools, communication, learning experiences, workplace behaviours and career opportunities. Some are visible. Others become apparent only when we listen to the people affected.

By combining professional expertise with lived experience, we help organisations ask better questions, challenge assumptions and make practical changes.

A principle that guides our work

Design WITH people.
Not simply FOR people.

Performance means having the opportunity to contribute, develop, progress and fulfil your potential.

Awareness→Understanding→Accessibility→Inclusion→Performance
What makes us different

Three perspectives.
One shared purpose.

Leadership

Powerbase brings experience in leadership development, communication, learning, behaviour and organisational capability. We help leaders translate inclusive intentions into everyday decisions and actions.

Technology

Our partnership with YouApps brings practical accessibility technology into the conversation, demonstrating how thoughtful digital design can remove barriers and support greater independence.

Lived experience

Our accessibility partner brings personal insight as a Person of Determination, alongside experience developing accessible applications. This connects organisational intentions with the realities people encounter.

Leadership + Technology + Lived Experience = Inclusive Performance

Your starting point

How accessible and inclusive is your organisation?

Our Access Check offers a short opportunity to reflect on current practice across spaces, tools, people and career development.

16 questions. Four areas. Your Access Snapshot. Identify strengths, visibility gaps and priorities for further exploration.

A self-reflection tool, rather than an audit or certification. Responses stay in this page and are not sent to Powerbase or stored.

Open the 16-question Access Check

Answer based on current practice. Choose “Don’t know” when you do not have enough information.

Spaces

1. Our physical environments are accessible to people with different mobility and sensory needs.
2. Our meeting, learning and event spaces enable people with different needs to participate comfortably.
3. Accessibility is considered when we design or modify employee and customer environments.
4. We consider factors such as lighting, noise, signage, navigation and sensory load.

Tools

5. Accessibility is considered when we select websites, apps, software and digital tools.
6. Important documents, presentations and communications are designed to be easy to access and understand.
7. People can access assistive technology or accessibility features when they need them.
8. We test whether our digital systems and information work effectively for people with different needs.

People

9. Our leaders understand the role accessibility plays in inclusion and performance.
10. People would feel comfortable raising an accessibility barrier or asking for support.
11. Accessibility is considered in recruitment, onboarding, communication, learning and development.
12. People with lived experience are involved when accessibility improvements are being considered.

Career Development & Progression

13. Employees with disabilities / People of Determination have career conversations that explore their strengths, aspirations and development needs.
14. Learning, mentoring, coaching and stretch opportunities are accessible to employees with different needs, with adjustments available where required.
15. Promotion and progression decisions use clear, fair criteria and consider how barriers or assumptions may affect employees with different needs.
16. We review whether employees with disabilities / People of Determination can access development and progression opportunities, and act on barriers identified.
